title: finding(layout): `useAppShellBranding` restores the tab title on unmount but never the favicon — objectui#8637 fixed one half and left the other as the lone survivor of the route-keyed reset
body:
Path: none | 标签页标题恢复不对称 | 装饰性

Filed by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat (PM session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`) while closing objectui#8637, whose dev measured the shape and correctly declined to file it on a code reading alone. ⛔ Not graded here.

## The asymmetry, read on the merged ref

objectui `origin/main` `0febe1a59` (PR objectui#10034's merge commit) at 2026-09-19T19:27Z, verified by the filing seat:

`packages/layout/src/AppShell.tsx`, inside `useAppShellBranding` — one effect, two branded writes, **one restore**:

| write | set while mounted | restored on unmount / change |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `document.title` | yes | ✅ **yes** — the effect captures the previous title and puts it back (objectui#8637) |
| the favicon (`link.href = branding.favicon`) | yes | ⛔ **no** — the cleanup restores the title only |

## ⭐ Why this is worth a card now, when it was not before

Before objectui#8637, **both** halves had the same hole, and the same thing put **both** back: `apps/console`'s route-keyed re-apply, which reassigned the runtime favicon (and, as the defect objectui#8637 fixed, the bare product name) on every navigation.

objectui#8637 gave the title a proper scoped restore and removed the title half of that route-keyed write. ⇒ The favicon is now the **lone survivor** of the old shape, and what puts it back is still only that re-apply — `apps/console/src/components/FaviconSync.tsx`, which is gated:

```
const faviconUrl = getFaviconUrl();
if (faviconUrl) {
  // reassign link.href
}
```

⇒ **On a deployment with no operator favicon configured, `getFaviconUrl()` is falsy, the re-apply is a no-op, and a branded app's favicon outlives the app** — it stays on the tab after the user leaves that app, with nothing to put the runtime one back.

## ⚠️ What is NOT claimed

⛔ **No browser reading was taken**, by the dev or by this seat. This is a code-path reading: the condition above is stated as the condition that would make it a defect, ⛔ not as an observed one. objectui#8637's own history is the reason to say this plainly — that card's fix shape was decided by a browser reading (`step 3`, the leave-the-app case) that a static reading did not give, and the same could be true here in either direction.

⛔ It is also not a claim that the favicon *should* be restored. The title's restore was justified by a measured revert-on-navigation; whether a favicon deserves the same scoping is a smaller question that has not been asked.

## 查重词

`favicon` · `useAppShellBranding` · `restore` · `unmount` · `branding.favicon`
